sentences.text: % 18.09.2023 [The proceeding has been conducted through Hybrid mode] CRL.M.A. 25235/2023 (Exemption)

1. Exemption allowed subject to just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

This petition under Article 226/227 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short "Cr.P.C.") has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing No.0690/2021 under Sections 498A/406 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "IPC") registered at Police Station Dabri and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom on the basis of settlement agreement dated 25.08.2023.
This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text:
1 4. Learned counsel appearing for the parties submit that the disputes between the parties have been amicably resolved by way of a settlement agreement recorded vide the Settlement Deed dated 25.08.2023.
5.

According to the terms of settlement, the petitioner No. 1 is to pay to respondent No.2 a sum of Rs.3,50,000/- towards full and final settlement which includes all claims in lieu of istridhan, dowry articles, past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony.
It is submitted that Rs.2,50,000/- has already been paid in the interregnum.
A sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is being paid today to the respondent No.2 in Court by way of DD No. 125702 dated 16.09.2023 Canara Bank Delhi Kingsway (GTB Nagar) Branch, Delhi.

entities.text: Canara Bank Delhi Kingsway (GTB Nagar) Branch
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 6. Respondent No.2 who is present in person, affirms the receipt of the same.
7. IO is present in person and identifies the parties appearing before this Court.
8. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner hands over the Bench a photocopy of the decree of divorce dated 28.01.2023.
The same is taken on record.
9. This Court has interacted with the respondent No.2 who submits that she has no further claims and disputes qua the petitioners.
She also submits that she has no objection in case the aforesaid FIR is quashed.
10. This Court has perused the terms of settlement agreement and they appear to be lawful.
The parties are bound by the terms of the settlement.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/09/2023 at 21:21:06 11.

After observing that the disputes are arising from matrimonial ties, this Court is of the considered opinion that no purpose would be served in continuing with the FIR in question and the further criminal proceedings and it would be in the interest of justice as also of the parties and the society that quietus is put to such disputes.
12. In view of the above, FIR No.0690/2021 under Sections 498A/406 IPC registered at Police Station Dabri and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are hereby quashed.
13. The petition stands disposed of.
TUSHAR RAO GEDELA, J SEPTEMBER 18, 2023/ms
